verses.sanskrit: पक्वाशयकटीसक्थिश्रोत्रास्थिस्पर्शनेन्द्रियम् । स्थानं वातस्य तत्रापि पक्वाधानं विशेषतः ॥१॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 1 identifies the principal seats of Vata, Pitta and Kapha and their especially important locations.

verses.sanskrit: नाभिरामाशयः स्वेदो लसीका रुधिरं रसः । दृक्स्पर्शनं च पित्तस्य नाभिरत्र विशेषतः ॥२॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 2 identifies the principal seats of Vata, Pitta and Kapha and their especially important locations.

verses.sanskrit: उरःकण्ठशिरःक्लोमपर्वाण्यामाशयो रसः । मेदो घ्राणं च जिह्वा च कफस्य सुतरामुरः ॥३॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 3 identifies the principal seats of Vata, Pitta and Kapha and their especially important locations.

verses.sanskrit: प्राणादिभेदात्पञ्चात्मा वायुः । प्राणोऽत्र मूर्धगः । उरःकण्ठचरो बुद्धिहृदयेन्द्रियचित्तधृक् ॥४॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 4 explains the five functional subdivisions of Vata and their sites and principal actions.

verses.sanskrit: ष्ठीवनक्षवथूद्गारनिःश्वासान्नप्रवेशकृत् ॥५॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 5 explains the five functional subdivisions of Vata and their sites and principal actions.

verses.sanskrit: उरः स्थानमुदानस्य नासानाभिगलांश्चरेत् । वाक्प्रवृत्तिप्रयत्नोर्जाबलवर्णस्मृतिक्रियः ॥६॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 6 explains the five functional subdivisions of Vata and their sites and principal actions.

verses.sanskrit: व्यानो हृदि स्थितः कृत्स्नदेहचारी महाजवः । गत्यपक्षेपणोत्क्षेपनिमेषोन्मेषणादिकाः प्रायः सर्वाः क्रियास्तस्मिन् प्रतिबद्धाः शरीरिणाम् ॥७॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 7 explains the five functional subdivisions of Vata and their sites and principal actions.

verses.sanskrit: समानोऽग्निसमीपस्थः कोष्ठे चरति सर्वतः । अन्नं गृह्णाति पचति विवेचयति मुञ्चति ॥८॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 8 explains the five functional subdivisions of Vata and their sites and principal actions.

verses.sanskrit: अपानोऽपानगः श्रोणिवस्तिमेढ्रोरुगोचरः । शुक्रार्तवशकृन्मूत्रगर्भनिष्क्रमणक्रियः ॥९॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 9 explains the five functional subdivisions of Vata and their sites and principal actions.

verses.sanskrit: तत्र पक्वामाशयमध्यगं पञ्चमहाभूतात्मकत्वेऽपि यत्तैजसगुणोदयात् । त्यक्तद्रवत्वं पाकादिकर्मणानलशब्दितम् ॥१०॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 10 explains the five functional subdivisions of Pitta and their sites and actions.

verses.sanskrit: पचत्यन्नं विभजते सारकिट्टौ पृथक् तथा । तत्रस्थमेव पित्तानां शेषाणामप्यनुग्रहम् ॥११॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 11 explains the five functional subdivisions of Pitta and their sites and actions.

verses.sanskrit: करोति बलदानेन पाचकं नाम तत्स्मृतम् ॥१२॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 12 explains the five functional subdivisions of Pitta and their sites and actions.

verses.sanskrit: आमाशयस्थं तु रञ्जकम् । रसस्य रञ्जनाद्रञ्जकम् ॥१३॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 13 explains the five functional subdivisions of Pitta and their sites and actions.

verses.sanskrit: हृदयस्थं साधकं बुद्धिमेधाभिमानाद्यैरभिप्रेतार्थसाधनात् ॥१४॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 14 explains the five functional subdivisions of Pitta and their sites and actions.

verses.sanskrit: दृक्स्थमालोचकं रूपालोचनात् ॥१५॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 15 explains the five functional subdivisions of Pitta and their sites and actions.

verses.sanskrit: त्वक्स्थं भ्राजकं भ्राजनात्त्वचः ॥१६॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 16 explains the five functional subdivisions of Pitta and their sites and actions.

verses.sanskrit: उरःस्थः स त्रिकस्य स्ववीर्यतः हृदयस्यान्नवीर्याच्च तत्स्थ एवाम्बुकर्मणा । कफधाम्नां च शेषाणां यत्करोत्यवलम्बनम् । अतोऽवलम्बकः श्लेष्मा ॥१७॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 17 explains the five functional subdivisions of Kapha and their sites and actions.

verses.sanskrit: यस्त्वामाशयसंस्थितः सोऽन्नसङ्घातक्लेदनात् क्लेदकः ॥१८॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 18 explains the five functional subdivisions of Kapha and their sites and actions.

verses.sanskrit: रसनास्थायी सम्यग्रसबोधनाद्बोधकः ॥१९॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 19 explains the five functional subdivisions of Kapha and their sites and actions.

verses.sanskrit: शिरस्थश्चक्षुरादीन्द्रियतर्पणात्तर्पकः ॥२०॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 20 explains the five functional subdivisions of Kapha and their sites and actions.

verses.sanskrit: पर्वस्थोऽस्थिसन्धिश्लेषणाच्छ्लेषकः ॥२१॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 21 explains the five functional subdivisions of Kapha and their sites and actions.

verses.sanskrit: चयो वृद्धिः स्वधाम्न्येव प्रद्वेषो वृद्धिहेतुषु । विपरीतगुणेच्छा च ॥२२॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 22 explains Chaya, Kopa and Shama of dosha and the characteristic signs of these stages.

verses.sanskrit: कोपस्तून्मार्गगामिता । लिङ्गानां दर्शनं स्वेषामस्वास्थ्यं रोगसम्भवः ॥२३॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 23 explains Chaya, Kopa and Shama of dosha and the characteristic signs of these stages.

verses.sanskrit: स्वस्थानस्थस्य समता विकारासम्भवः शमः ॥२४॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 24 explains Chaya, Kopa and Shama of dosha and the characteristic signs of these stages.

verses.sanskrit: चीयते लघुरूक्षाभिरोषधीभिः समीरणः । तद्विधस्तद्विधे देहे कालस्यौष्ण्यान्न कुप्यति ॥२५॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 25 explains seasonal dosha Chaya, Prakopa and Prashama and how diet and behavior can alter seasonal patterns.

verses.sanskrit: अद्भिरम्लविपाकाभिरोषधीभिश्च तादृशं पित्तं याति चयं कोपं न तु कालस्य शैत्यतः ॥२६॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 26 explains seasonal dosha Chaya, Prakopa and Prashama and how diet and behavior can alter seasonal patterns.

verses.sanskrit: चीयते स्निग्धशीताभिरुदकौषधिभिः कफः । तुल्येऽपि काले देहे च स्कन्नत्वान्न प्रकुप्यति ॥२७॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 27 explains seasonal dosha Chaya, Prakopa and Prashama and how diet and behavior can alter seasonal patterns.

verses.sanskrit: इति कालस्वभावोऽयमाहारादिवशात्पुनः । चयादीन् यान्ति सद्योऽपि दोषाः कालेऽपि वा न तु ॥२८॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 28 explains seasonal dosha Chaya, Prakopa and Prashama and how diet and behavior can alter seasonal patterns.

verses.sanskrit: व्याप्नोति सहसा देहमापादतलमस्तकम् । निवर्तते तु कुपितो मलोऽल्पाल्पं जलौघवत् ॥२९॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 29 explains the rapid spread and slower reversal of aggravated doshas and introduces general principles because diseases are innumerable.

verses.sanskrit: नानारूपैरसङ्ख्येयैर्विकारैः कुपिता मलाः । तापयन्ति तनुं तस्मात्तद्धेत्वाकृतिसाधनम् ॥३०॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 30 explains the rapid spread and slower reversal of aggravated doshas and introduces general principles because diseases are innumerable.

verses.sanskrit: शक्यं नैकैकशो वक्तुमतः सामान्यमुच्यते ॥३१॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 31 explains the rapid spread and slower reversal of aggravated doshas and introduces general principles because diseases are innumerable.

verses.sanskrit: दोषा एव हि सर्वेषां रोगाणामेककारणम् । यथा पक्षी परिपतन् सर्वतः सर्वमप्यहः ॥३२॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 32 establishes doshas as the fundamental basis of disease and explains that disease manifestations remain within the framework of the three doshas.

verses.sanskrit: छायामत्येति नात्मीयां यथा वा कृत्स्नमप्यदः । विकारजातं विविधं त्रीन् गुणान्नातिवर्तते ॥३३॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 33 establishes doshas as the fundamental basis of disease and explains that disease manifestations remain within the framework of the three doshas.

verses.sanskrit: तथा स्वधातुवैषम्यनिमित्तमपि सर्वदा । विकारजातं त्रीन्दोषान्नातिवर्तते ॥३४॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 34 establishes doshas as the fundamental basis of disease and explains that disease manifestations remain within the framework of the three doshas.

verses.sanskrit: तेषां कोपे तु कारणमर्थैरसात्म्यैः संयोगः कालः कर्म च दुष्कृतम् । हीनातिमिथ्यायोगेन भिद्यते तत्पुनस्त्रिधा ॥३५॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 35 explains the three broad causes of dosha aggravation: unsuitable sense-object contact, time/season and improper action, each having three modes.

verses.sanskrit: हीनोऽर्थेनेन्द्रियस्याल्पः संयोगः स्वेन नैव वा । अतियोगोऽतिसंसर्गः सूक्ष्मभासुरभैरवम् ॥३६॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 36 explains Hina, Ati and Mithya Yoga of sense objects and Kala, with examples of excessive, deficient and inappropriate exposure.

verses.sanskrit: अत्यासन्नातिदूरस्थं विप्रियं विकृतादि च । यदक्ष्णा वीक्ष्यते रूपं मिथ्यायोगः स दारुणः ॥३७॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 37 explains Hina, Ati and Mithya Yoga of sense objects and Kala, with examples of excessive, deficient and inappropriate exposure.

verses.sanskrit: एवमत्युच्चपूत्यादीनिन्द्रियार्थान् यथायथं विद्यात् । कालस्तु शीतोष्णवर्षाभेदात्त्रिधा मतः ॥३८॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 38 explains Hina, Ati and Mithya Yoga of sense objects and Kala, with examples of excessive, deficient and inappropriate exposure.

verses.sanskrit: स हीनो हीनशीतादिरतियोगोऽतिलक्षणः । मिथ्यायोगस्तु निर्दिष्टो विपरीतस्वलक्षणः ॥३९॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 39 explains Hina, Ati and Mithya Yoga of sense objects and Kala, with examples of excessive, deficient and inappropriate exposure.

verses.sanskrit: कायवाक्चित्तभेदेन कर्मापि विभजेत् त्रिधा । कायादिकर्मणो हीना प्रवृत्तिर्हीनसंज्ञकः ॥४०॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 40 explains Hina, Ati and Mithya Yoga of bodily, verbal and mental activity and their role in dosha aggravation.

verses.sanskrit: अतियोगोऽतिवृत्तिस्तु वेगोदीरणधारणम् । विषमाङ्गक्रियारम्भपतनस्खलनादिकम् ॥४१॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 41 explains Hina, Ati and Mithya Yoga of bodily, verbal and mental activity and their role in dosha aggravation.

verses.sanskrit: भाषणं सामिभुक्तस्य रागद्वेषभयादि च । कर्म प्राणातिपातादि दशधा यच्च निन्दितम् ॥४२॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 42 explains Hina, Ati and Mithya Yoga of bodily, verbal and mental activity and their role in dosha aggravation.

verses.sanskrit: मिथ्यायोगः समस्तोऽसाविह वामुत्र वा कृतम् । निदानमेतद्दोषाणां कुपितास्तेन नैकधा ॥४३॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 43 explains Hina, Ati and Mithya Yoga of bodily, verbal and mental activity and their role in dosha aggravation.

verses.sanskrit: कुर्वन्ति विविधान् व्याधीन् शाखाकोष्ठास्थिसन्धिषु ॥४४॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 44 describes the three Rogamargas—external, internal and middle—and the diseases characteristically associated with each pathway.

verses.sanskrit: शाखा रक्तादयस्त्वक्च बाह्यरोगायनं हि तत् । तदाश्रया मशव्यङ्गगण्डालज्यर्बुदादयः ॥४५॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 45 describes the three Rogamargas—external, internal and middle—and the diseases characteristically associated with each pathway.

verses.sanskrit: बहिर्भागाश्च दुर्नामगुल्मशोफादयो गदाः ॥४६॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 46 describes the three Rogamargas—external, internal and middle—and the diseases characteristically associated with each pathway.

verses.sanskrit: अन्तःकोष्ठो महास्रोत आमपक्वाशयाश्रयः । तत्स्थानाः छर्द्यतीसारकासश्वासोदरज्वराः ॥४७॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 47 describes the three Rogamargas—external, internal and middle—and the diseases characteristically associated with each pathway.

verses.sanskrit: अन्तर्भागं च शोफार्शोगुल्मविसर्पविद्रधि ॥४८॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 48 describes the three Rogamargas—external, internal and middle—and the diseases characteristically associated with each pathway.

verses.sanskrit: शिरोहृदयवस्त्यादिमर्माण्यस्थ्नां च सन्धयः । तन्निबद्धाः सिरास्नायुकण्डराद्याश्च मध्यमः ॥४९॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 49 describes the three Rogamargas—external, internal and middle—and the diseases characteristically associated with each pathway.

verses.sanskrit: रोगमार्गः स्थितास्तत्र यक्ष्मपक्षवधार्दिताः । मूर्धादिरोगाः सन्ध्यस्थित्रिकशूलग्रहादयः ॥५०॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 50 describes the three Rogamargas—external, internal and middle—and the diseases characteristically associated with each pathway.

verses.sanskrit: स्रंसव्यासव्यधस्वापासादरुक्तोदभेदनम् ॥५१॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 51 gives the classical signs of Vata, Pitta and Kapha increase.

verses.sanskrit: सङ्गाङ्गभङ्गसङ्कोचवर्तहर्षणतर्पणम् । कम्पपारुष्यसौषिर्यशोषस्पन्दनवेष्टनम् ॥५२॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 52 gives the classical signs of Vata, Pitta and Kapha increase.

verses.sanskrit: स्तम्भः कषायरसता वर्णः श्यावोऽरुणोऽपि वा । कर्माणि वायोः ॥५३॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 53 gives the classical signs of Vata, Pitta and Kapha increase.

verses.sanskrit: पित्तस्य दाहरागोष्मपाकिताः । स्वेदः क्लेदः स्रुतिः कोथः सदनं मूर्च्छनं मदः ॥५४॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 54 gives the classical signs of Vata, Pitta and Kapha increase.

verses.sanskrit: कटुकाम्लौ रसौ वर्णः पाण्डुरारुणवर्जितः ॥५५॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 55 gives the classical signs of Vata, Pitta and Kapha increase.

verses.sanskrit: श्लेष्मणः स्नेहकाठिन्यकण्डूशीतत्वगौरवम् । बन्धोपलेपस्तैमित्यशोफापक्त्यतिनिद्रताः ॥५६॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 56 gives the classical signs of Vata, Pitta and Kapha increase.

verses.sanskrit: वर्णः श्वेतो रसौ स्वादुलवणौ चिरकारिता ॥५७॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 57 gives the classical signs of Vata, Pitta and Kapha increase.

verses.sanskrit: इत्यशेषामयव्यापि यदुक्तं दोषलक्षणम् । दर्शनाद्यैरवहितस्तत्सम्यगुपलक्षयेत् ॥५८॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 58 emphasizes careful observation, clinical experience and the limits of relying on textual nomenclature alone.

verses.sanskrit: व्याध्यवस्थाविभागज्ञः पश्यन्नार्तान् प्रतिक्षणम् । अभ्यासात्प्राप्यते दृष्टिः कर्मसिद्धिप्रकाशिनी ॥५९॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 59 emphasizes careful observation, clinical experience and the limits of relying on textual nomenclature alone.

verses.sanskrit: रत्नादिसदसज्ज्ञानं न शास्त्रादेव जायते ॥६०॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 60 emphasizes careful observation, clinical experience and the limits of relying on textual nomenclature alone.

verses.sanskrit: दृष्टापचारजः कश्चित् कश्चित् पूर्वापराधजः । तत्सङ्कराद्भवत्यन्यो व्याधिरेवं त्रिधा स्मृतः ॥६१॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 61 classifies diseases into Dosha-born, Karma-born and mixed Dosha-Karma types and gives their general resolution principles.

verses.sanskrit: यथानिदानं दोषोत्थः कर्मजो हेतुभिर्विना । महारम्भोऽल्पके हेतावातङ्को दोषकर्मजः ॥६२॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 62 classifies diseases into Dosha-born, Karma-born and mixed Dosha-Karma types and gives their general resolution principles.

verses.sanskrit: विपक्षशीलनात्पूर्वः कर्मजः कर्मसङ्क्षयात् । गच्छत्युभयजन्मा तु दोषकर्मक्षयात्क्षयम् ॥६३॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 63 classifies diseases into Dosha-born, Karma-born and mixed Dosha-Karma types and gives their general resolution principles.

verses.sanskrit: द्विधा स्वतन्त्रपरतन्त्रत्वाद्व्याधयोऽन्त्याः पुनर्द्विधा । पूर्वजाः पूर्वरूपाख्या जाताः पश्चादुपद्रवाः ॥६४॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 64 explains independent and dependent diseases, premonitory features and complications, with guidance on prioritizing treatment.

verses.sanskrit: यथास्वजन्मोपशयाः स्वतन्त्राः स्पष्टलक्षणाः । विपरीतास्ततोऽन्ये तु ॥६५॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 65 explains independent and dependent diseases, premonitory features and complications, with guidance on prioritizing treatment.

verses.sanskrit: विद्यादेवं मलानपि । तान् लक्षयेदवहितो विकुर्वाणान् ॥६६॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 66 explains independent and dependent diseases, premonitory features and complications, with guidance on prioritizing treatment.

verses.sanskrit: तेषां प्रधानप्रशमे प्रशमोऽशाम्यतस्तथा । पश्चाच्चिकित्सेत्तूर्णं बलवन्तमुपद्रवम् ॥६७॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 67 explains independent and dependent diseases, premonitory features and complications, with guidance on prioritizing treatment.

verses.sanskrit: व्याधिनामाकुशलो न जिह्रीयात्कदाचन । न हि सर्वविकाराणां नामतोऽस्ति ध्रुवा स्थितिः ॥६८॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 68 explains that the same aggravated dosha can produce different diseases in different sites and therefore treatment must consider disease, site and causative factors.

verses.sanskrit: स एव कुपितो दोषः समुत्थानविशेषतः । स्थानान्तराणि च प्राप्य विकारान् कुरुते बहून् ॥६९॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 69 explains that the same aggravated dosha can produce different diseases in different sites and therefore treatment must consider disease, site and causative factors.

verses.sanskrit: तस्माद्विकारप्रकृतीरधिष्ठानान्तराणि च । बुद्ध्वा हेतुविशेषांश्च शीघ्रं कुर्यादुपक्रमम् ॥७०॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 70 explains that the same aggravated dosha can produce different diseases in different sites and therefore treatment must consider disease, site and causative factors.

verses.sanskrit: दूष्यं देशं बलं कालमनलं प्रकृतिं वयः । सत्त्वं सात्म्यं तथाहारमवस्थाश्च पृथग्विधाः ॥७१॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 71 lists the patient and disease factors that must be assessed before selecting dosha, medicine and treatment.

verses.sanskrit: सूक्ष्मसूक्ष्माः समीक्ष्यैषां दोषौषधनिरूपणे । यो वर्तते चिकित्सायां न स स्खलति जातुचित् ॥७२॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 72 lists the patient and disease factors that must be assessed before selecting dosha, medicine and treatment.

verses.sanskrit: गुर्वल्पव्याधिसंस्थानं सत्त्वदेहबलाबलात् । दृश्यतेऽप्यन्यथाकारं तस्मिन्नवहितो भवेत् ॥७३॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 73 lists the patient and disease factors that must be assessed before selecting dosha, medicine and treatment.

verses.sanskrit: गुरुं लघुमिति व्याधिं कल्पयंस्तु भिषग्ब्रुवः । अल्पदोषाकलनया पथ्ये विप्रतिपद्यते ॥७४॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 74 warns against underestimating or overestimating disease severity and against inadequate or excessive purification.

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽल्पमल्पवीर्यं वा गुरुर्व्याधौ प्रयोजितम् । उदीरयेत्तरां रोगान् संशोधनमयोगतः ॥७५॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 75 warns against underestimating or overestimating disease severity and against inadequate or excessive purification.

verses.sanskrit: शोधनं त्वतियोगेन विपरीतं विपर्यये । क्षिणुयान्न मलानेव केवलं वपुरस्यति ॥७६॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 76 warns against underestimating or overestimating disease severity and against inadequate or excessive purification.

verses.sanskrit: अतोऽभियुक्तः सततं सर्वमालोच्य सर्वथा । तथा युञ्जीत भैषज्यमारोग्याय यथा ध्रुवम् ॥७७॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 77 concludes with the physician's duty to assess all factors carefully and introduces the numerical classification of dosha increase/decrease combinations.

verses.sanskrit: वक्ष्यन्तेऽतः परं दोषा वृद्धिक्षयविभेदतः । पृथक् त्रीन् विद्धि संसर्गस्त्रिधा तत्र तु तान्नव ॥७८॥
verses.student_meaning: Verse 78 concludes with the physician's duty to assess all factors carefully and introduces the numerical classification of dosha increase/decrease combinations.

supplementary_half_verse.sanskrit: संसर्गाद्रसरुधिरादिभिस्तथैषां दोषांस्तु क्षयसमताविवृद्धिभेदैः । आनन्त्यं तरतमयोगतश्च यातान् जानीयादवहितमानसो यथास्वम् ॥
supplementary_half_verse.student_meaning: The concluding half-verse explains that combinations involving Rasa, Rakta and other factors, together with degrees of dosha depletion, balance and increase, become innumerable; the physician should recognize them attentively from their features.

learning_outcomes: Identify the principal seats of Vata, Pitta and Kapha.
Explain the five functional subdivisions of each dosha and their sites/actions.
Explain Chaya, Kopa and Shama and seasonal dosha variation.
Explain Hina, Ati and Mithya Yoga of sense objects, Kala and Karma.
Describe Bahya, Abhyantara and Madhyama Rogamarga.
Recognize classical signs of dosha Vriddhi.
Classify diseases as Dosha-born, Karma-born, mixed, independent and dependent.
Apply the patient-assessment factors used for rational treatment selection.
Explain the numerical framework of dosha combination and its clinical implication.
exam_focus: Dosha sthana and five subtypes of each dosha.
Functions of Prana, Udana, Vyana, Samana and Apana.
Pachaka, Ranjaka, Sadhaka, Alochaka and Bhrajaka Pitta.
Avalambaka, Kledaka, Bodhaka, Tarpaka and Shleshaka Kapha.
Trividha Nidana: Artha, Kala and Karma with Hina-Ati-Mithya Yoga.
Three Rogamargas and examples of diseases.
Signs of Vata, Pitta and Kapha Vriddhi.
Clinical assessment factors and rational treatment selection.
Dosha combination enumeration in the concluding verses.

source_text.verification_note: Chapter 12 runs through verse 78 and has a traditional concluding half-verse (78½) before the chapter colophon. The half-verse is preserved separately so the 78 numbered verses remain structurally countable.

revision_summary: Memorize dosha locations and the five subtypes with one key function each.
Learn Hina, Ati and Mithya Yoga under Artha, Kala and Karma.
Draw the three Rogamargas with representative diseases.
Practice identifying Vata, Pitta and Kapha Vriddhi signs.
Revise Trividha Roga and Svatantra/Paratantra classifications.
Use the diagnostic-factor list as a clinical reasoning checklist.
Understand the 62 pathological combinations and the 63rd healthy equilibrium state.
